title: Quasi-compact complement of finitely presented module support
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a $B$-module admitting an exact sequence $B^u\to B^v\to M\to0$ for finite integers $u,v\ge0$ (a finitely presented module). In $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put $\operatorname{Supp}_B(M)=\{\mathfrak p: M_{\mathfrak p}\ne0\}$, where $M_{\mathfrak p}$ consists of fractions $m/s$ for $s\notin\mathfrak p$, with the usual equality after multiplication by another element outside $\mathfrak p$. Then $\operatorname{Supp}_B(M)$ is closed and its complement is quasi-compact, meaning every cover of the complement by open subsets has a finite subcover.

proof.text: Fix the given presentation, write $q:B^v\to M$ for its surjection, and let $A$ be the $v\times u$ matrix of its first map in the coordinate bases. Thus $\ker q=\operatorname{im}A$. Put $m_j=q(e_j)$; these finitely many elements generate $M$. For each $v$-element subset $S$ of the $u$ columns put $d_S=\det(A^S)$, and let $I=(d_S)_S$. There are finitely many such subsets. If $v=0$, the presentation gives $M=0$, the unique empty minor is $1$, and $I=B$.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime and suppose $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$. Each $m_j/1=0$ gives $s_j\notin\mathfrak p$ with $s_jm_j=0$ by the fraction equality in the statement. Set $s=\prod_j s_j\notin\mathfrak p$ (empty product $1$). Then $q(se_j)=0$, so exactness supplies $c_j\in B^u$ with $Ac_j=se_j$. The matrix $C$ with columns $c_j$ satisfies $AC=s1_v$.

proof.text: Conversely, if $I\nsubseteq\mathfrak p$, some generator $d_S$ is outside $\mathfrak p$. Let $E_S:B^v\to B^u$ insert the selected coordinates, so $AE_S=A^S$. The adjugate identity gives $A(E_S\operatorname{adj}(A^S))=d_S1_v$. Applying $q$ shows $d_Sm_j=0$ for every $j$, hence $d_SM=0$. Since $d_S\notin\mathfrak p$, the localization fraction criterion gives $m/t=0$ for every $m/t\in M_{\mathfrak p}$ (use multiplier $d_S$); thus $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$. Together with the preceding steps, $\operatorname{Supp}_B(M)=V(I)$. This is closed by the definition of the Zariski topology.

source.place: Tag 051B (algebra-lemma-support-finite-presentation-constructible), proof; expanded maximal-minor criterion using Tags 07DQ and 0F0K

proof.text: For any $f\in B$, the cited localization homeomorphism identifies $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B_f$, and the cited spectrum compactness applies to the commutative ring $B_f$. To check compactness explicitly, pull any open cover of $D(f)$ back through this homeomorphism, choose a finite subcover of $\operatorname{Spec}B_f$, and push its members back. Hence every $D(f)$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 051B, last sentence, using Tag 00E4 (algebra-lemma-standard-open) and Tag 00E8 (algebra-lemma-quasi-compact)

proof.text: A prime contains $I=(d_S)_S$ precisely when it contains every $d_S$, so $\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus\operatorname{Supp}_B(M)=\bigcup_S D(d_S)$. For an arbitrary open cover of this union, its restriction to each $D(d_S)$ admits a finite subcover by the preceding step. Take the union of these finitely many finite choices to cover the entire complement. When there are no minors the union is empty and the empty subcover suffices. When $v=0$ it is $D(1)=\operatorname{Spec}B$.
